questions.q: What does this lesson say every capstone project in this chapter actually is?
options: A composition exercise — proving that earlier lessons' individual techniques combine on one real system, not a place where new theory is introduced
An entirely separate curriculum from the rest of the track
A test of memorization rather than application
A replacement for the retrospectives written after each project
questions.explain: Project 3 alone drew on Kappa architecture and idempotency, Eventstreams and windowing, MERGE INTO, and back-of-the-envelope estimation — all taught earlier in the track.

questions.q: Which courses in the 4-course Data Engineering track did Project 3 draw on, according to this wrap-up?
options: All four — this course's own Chapter 1, Fabric & Real-Time Analytics, Databricks & Delta Lake, and Data Engineering Foundations
Only this course, Career & Capstone
Only Databricks & Delta Lake
None — Project 3 introduced entirely new material
questions.explain: Kappa architecture and idempotency came from this course, Eventstreams and windowing from Fabric, MERGE INTO from Databricks, and estimation habits from Foundations.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a written retrospective matters more for a real-time streaming system than for a batch migration?
options: Real-time systems fail in ways that are harder to notice after the fact, so the retrospective is often the only place near-misses get recorded
Streaming systems never fail, so retrospectives are purely for documentation
Batch systems don't require retrospectives at all
Streaming retrospectives take less time to write
questions.explain: Because of how failures in real-time systems can go unnoticed, writing the retrospective down captures near-misses that might otherwise be lost.

questions.q: What's the "genuine turn" this lesson says the chapter is about to make?
options: From technical capstone projects to career-focused lessons on building a portfolio and telling a project story in an interview
From streaming systems back to batch systems
From this course back to earlier courses in the track
From written retrospectives to video retrospectives
questions.explain: Lessons 79 and 80 are explicitly not technical lessons — they turn the three completed capstone projects into portfolio material and interview stories.

questions.q: What raw material do the retrospectives from Projects 2 and 3 directly feed into?
options: The portfolio and interview-story lessons coming next in the chapter
A fourth capstone project not covered in this course
The DP-700 certification exam covered earlier in the track
Nothing — retrospectives are discarded once the project closes
questions.explain: The specific, honest answers written in each retrospective are exactly what gets reused when building a portfolio and preparing an interview walkthrough.
